name: Peach rose
lede: Peach rose is a dark, yellowish pink from Ridgway's 1912 plates, where it is named Orange-Vinaceous, and over-represented in paintings from India.

sections.title: A dusty pink, filed twice
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate XXVII, hue 5′′, tone b, scanned from an aged plate and so approximate, under the name Orange-Vinaceous [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it in its own red block [1]. Our color graph finds a separately recorded name, Peach Rose, at zero units of difference, an exact duplicate under a different name — the name this article leads with [2].

Its nearest distinct relatives in the graph are [[grecian-rose]], almost the same, and [[brownish-vinaceous]] and [[old-rose]], both close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Peach rose covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 147 works, more common than 51 per cent of our named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 12 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.6 times the archive's overall rate, and is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.5 times expected [4]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is 1230, nearly seven centuries before the name's own 1912 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].
